purpose: Per CEO R289 P0: Freeze the commercial mechanism. Sensor-health fallback becomes implementation module, not central invention claim, because 2026 prior art (US20260115436A1) is already strong in sensor-failure handling.
constitutional_basis: Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion. Article X — honest disclosure of what is and isn't novel.

frozen_commercial_mechanism.name: Rate-Limited Physiologic Conductance Control for Multi-Segment CSF Drainage
frozen_commercial_mechanism.central_claim: A bounded-rate conductance-control regime that, in computational tests, produces a materially different robustness envelope under sensor uncertainty compared to existing predictive closed-loop approaches.
frozen_commercial_mechanism.what_is_frozen: The bounded-rate conductance slew (2%/sec max) applied to multi-segment continuous redistribution is the central commercial mechanism.
frozen_commercial_mechanism.what_is_demoted: Sensor-health fallback is an implementation module, NOT the central invention claim. US20260115436A1 (2026) already covers sensor failure handling and fallback. We do not claim the fallback as our invention — we claim the BOUNDED RATE + MULTI-SEGMENT REDISTRIBUTION combination.

buyer_facing_technical_story.the_story: physiologic sensing → desired conductance → bounded conductance slew → continuous redistribution → hydraulic response
buyer_facing_technical_story.rationale: The technical story focuses on the TRANSFERABLE ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (bounded-rate conductance control), not on marketing language (AI/predictive/smart). The buyer's engineers can evaluate the principle; they cannot evaluate marketing language.

the_commercial_argument.our_proposed_contribution: A particular bounded-rate multi-segment conductance-control regime that, in our computational tests (225-run ablation, 5 seeds, 9 attacks), appears to produce a materially different robustness envelope under sensor uncertainty.
evidence_for_our_argument: V2.1 beats existing closed-loop approach by 2.1-2.9x on time-to-failure across 9 attack modes (5 seeds each)
Rate limiting is the dominant mechanism (41/45 ablation runs confirm criticality)
The advantage holds under sensor noise, dropout, fast/slow occlusion, model error, controller delay, actuator saturation
Multi_failure is the known catastrophic boundary (peak 69.8 mmHg — disclosed honestly)
what_we_are_NOT_arguing: NOT arguing we invented closed-loop shunt control
NOT arguing we invented sensor-failure fallback
NOT arguing we invented flow regulation
NOT arguing we invented physiologic sensing

module_1_core.name: Bounded-Rate Conductance Controller
module_1_core.parameters: max alpha change = 2%/sec, continuous redistribution (no hard isolation)
module_1_core.ablation_evidence: Critical on 41/45 runs. Mean ratio 0.65 without it.

module_2_implementation.name: Sensor-Health Fallback
module_2_implementation.rationale: US20260115436A1 already covers sensor failure handling. We use it as engineering hygiene, not as the invention.
module_2_implementation.parameters: freeze alpha when p_obs ≤ 0.5 or all-flow-zero, recover after 3 consecutive good samples

module_3_optional.name: Hysteresis Deadband
module_3_optional.status: OPTIONAL (conditionally useful under high controller latency)
module_3_optional.ablation_evidence: Critical only on controller_delay (0.70 ratio). Non-critical on 8/9 attacks.

module_4_optional.name: Drainage Floor
module_4_optional.status: OPTIONAL (V2.2 should relax during sensor dropout)
module_4_optional.ablation_evidence: Non-critical overall (1.22 ratio). Actually HELPS on sensor_dropout (2.98x). V2.2 design insight: relax floor during dropout.

module_5_optional.name: Alpha Floor (5% minimum)
module_5_optional.ablation_evidence: Non-critical (1.00 ratio, critical on only 1/45 runs)

why_this_freeze_matters.simpler_TTP: The TTP now leads with ONE principle (bounded-rate conductance control) instead of four interacting features. Easier for buyer to evaluate.
why_this_freeze_matters.honest_IP_position: We don't claim sensor-health fallback as our invention (US20260115436A1 covers it). We claim the bounded-rate + multi-segment combination.
why_this_freeze_matters.transferable: The bounded-rate principle is transferable to other fluidic medical systems (vascular, dialysis, infusion, respiratory). The sensor-health fallback is application-specific.
why_this_freeze_matters.defensible: The 225-run ablation provides quantitative evidence that rate limiting is the dominant mechanism. This is a technical argument, not a marketing claim.
